title: An early English moth score had a positive warmth slope in later England but uncertain slopes in Scotland in 1992-2015
abstract: We tested whether a moth catch composition score could transfer across time and regions. We learned 174 taxon weights from 300 English trap-months in 1992-2003. We fixed the weights before three tests. Models controlled trap by month, rain, sample count, mean sample date and linear time. The later English temperature slope was 0.233 training residual standard deviations per C, with a three-test interval of 0.024 to 0.441. Early and later Scottish slopes were 0.177 and 0.101; both intervals included zero. Catch-size control and trap trends kept the clear English slope. A twenty-night sample rule made it uncertain. The score shows limited transfer across time in England. Clear transfer across regions was not shown. Shared traps, correlated weather, few Scottish sites and species-specific capture limit inference. Intervals are conditional on the learned weights. We test no causal climate, air pollution or daily extreme effect. Code, aggregate results, model weights, source hashes, checks and retrieval instructions are included. Source and derived record databases remain outside the package.

display.caption: Fixed early-English score slopes in three test samples. Intervals account for three tests and are conditional on learned weights. Units are training residual standard deviations per C.
